1.title: CLAUDE.md, Rules, Slash Commands and Skills
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Claude dot M D, Rules, Slash Commands and Skills. This module covers task statements three point one to three point three: claude dot m d, rules, slash commands and skills. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. The Claude dot M D hierarchy: user, project and directory level, and who shares what. the at import syntax and the dot Claude rules folder to keep instructions modular; slash memory to diagnose. Slash commands and skills: where they live, and the frontmatter context: fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint. Path-specific rules with glob patterns, and when they beat directory-level files.

1.title: Case Check-In: A New Engineer at Birchwood Supply Gets Different Answers
1.text: Our running case is Birchwood Supply. A New Engineer at Birchwood Supply Gets Different Answers. A teammate joins and Claude Code ignores the team's coding standards. The standards sit in the lead developer's own home dot Claude, Claude dot M D. Another problem: the root file has grown to eight hundred lines, mixing testing, A P I (application programming interface) and deployment rules.

1.title: CLAUDE.md Files and Their Hierarchy
1.text: Claude dot M D Files and Their Hierarchy. Claude dot M D is a Markdown file of persistent instructions that Claude Code loads into context at the start of a session. User. Location: home dot Claude, Claude dot M D. Shared with the team?: No: applies only to you, not in version control. Project. Location: Claude dot M D at the repo root, or the dot Claude Claude dot M D file. Shared with the team?: Yes, through version control. Directory. Location: Claude dot M D inside a subdirectory. Shared with the team?: Yes (committed); applies to work in that directory.

1.title: CLAUDE.md Files and Their Hierarchy, continued
1.text: Claude dot M D Files and Their Hierarchy, continued. The figure shows this: Claude dot M D levels: user (personal, not shared), project (shared via version control) and directory (shared, scoped to a folder); loaded files are combined into the context. Diagnosis rule: a new teammate not receiving instructions usually means those instructions live in user-level configuration instead of project-level configuration. Files are combined, not overridden: more specific content is simply added to the context. Keep each file short (the guidance is under about two hundred lines) and avoid contradictions.

1.title: Keeping it modular
1.text: Keeping it modular. the at import syntax: reference other files from a Claude dot M D so each package pulls in only the standards that apply to it (for example @docs or standards or testing dot M D). Paths resolve relative to the file that contains the import. the dot Claude rules folder: split a large Claude dot M D into topic files such as testing dot M D, api-conventions dot M D, deployment dot M D. slash memory shows which memory files are loaded and lets you open them: use it to diagnose inconsistent behavior across sessions. Exam tip: "Instructions apply for me but not for a teammate" to user versus project level. "One huge file" to split into the dot Claude rules folder topic files or the at import syntax.

1.title: Keeping it modular, continued
1.text: Keeping it modular, continued. Current documentation adds: a Claude dot local dot M D for private project preferences (gitignored); managed policy Claude dot M D for organizations; Claude dot M D files in directories above the working directory load at launch while those in subdirectories load on demand when Claude works with files there; imports can nest up to four levels. Claude dot M D is context, not enforcement: for guaranteed behavior use hooks (Module three). As of eight November two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: Slash Commands and Skills
1.text: Slash Commands and Skills. Custom slash command. Project-scoped: the dot Claude commands folder (in the repo, shared when teammates clone or pull). User-scoped: home dot Claude commands (personal). Skill. Project-scoped: a skill folder with a Skill dot M D file (shared). User-scoped: home dot Claude skills less than name greater than or Skill dot M D (personal). A skill is a folder with a Skill dot M D file: Yammel (a human-readable data format for configuration) frontmatter plus instructions, used on demand for a task-specific workflow.

1.title: Slash Commands and Skills, continued
1.text: Slash Commands and Skills, continued. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Slash Commands and Skills, continued
1.text: Slash Commands and Skills, continued. context: fork. Runs the skill in an isolated sub-agent context, so verbose output (codebase analysis) or exploratory context (brainstorming alternatives) does not pollute the main conversation. allowed-tools. Restricts tool access during skill execution (for example only file-write or read-only tools) to avoid destructive actions. argument-hint. Prompts the developer for required parameters when they invoke the skill without arguments.

1.title: Slash Commands and Skills, continued
1.text: Slash Commands and Skills, continued. The figure shows this: A skill is a Skill dot M D with frontmatter: context fork isolates its output, allowed-tools limits its tools, argument-hint prompts for parameters. Personal variants: to customize a team skill for yourself, create your own in home dot Claude skills with a different name, so teammates are unaffected.

1.title: Skills versus CLAUDE.md
1.text: Skills versus Claude dot M D. Loaded. Claude dot M D: Always. Skill or command: On demand, when invoked (or chosen by Claude for a matching task). Use for. Claude dot M D: Universal standards that apply to nearly every task. Skill or command: Task-specific workflows (review checklist, release steps, migrations).

1.title: Skills versus CLAUDE.md, continued
1.text: Skills versus Claude dot M D, continued. In current Claude Code, custom commands have been merged into skills: a file at the dot Claude commands folderdeploy dot M D and a skill at the dot Claude skills folderdeploy or Skill dot M D both create or deploy; existing command files keep working, and if both exist the skill wins. Note that allowed-tools pre-approves the listed tools (no permission prompt) and does not by itself forbid other tools; use disallowed Tools or permission rules to restrict. Skill descriptions are always in context; the full content loads when the skill is used. As of eight November two thousand twenty-six. For the exam, answer as the guide teaches (commands in the dot Claude commands folder, allowed-tools to limit tools). Exam tip: Always-needed standards go in Claude dot M D; task workflows go in skills or commands; verbose or exploratory skills use context: fork.

1.title: Path-Specific Rules
1.text: Path-Specific Rules. Problem: coding conventions differ by area (React components, A P I handlers, database models) and test files sit next to the code they test throughout the repository. A directory-level Claude dot M D cannot cover files spread across many directories. Solution: put rule files in the dot Claude rules folder with Yammel frontmatter paths holding glob patterns. The rule loads only when Claude works with a matching file.

1.title: Path-Specific Rules, continued
1.text: Path-Specific Rules, continued. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Path-Specific Rules, continued
1.text: Path-Specific Rules, continued. The figure shows this: Path-specific rules: a glob pattern in the rule's frontmatter loads the convention only when a matching file is edited, wherever it lives.

1.title: Path-Specific Rules, continued
1.text: Path-Specific Rules, continued. Path-specific rule (paths: globs). Conventions follow file type or pattern, spread across directories (all test files), and should apply automatically and deterministically. Directory-level Claude dot M D. Conventions belong to one directory tree. Skill. A workflow the developer invokes on demand; not automatic by file path. One big root Claude dot M D. Small projects; unreliable when areas differ (relies on the model inferring which section applies). Advantages: less irrelevant context and fewer tokens, because the rule is absent until needed. Exam tip: Conventions tied to file type and scattered across directories (tests) call for path-specific rules with globs, not many directory Claude dot M D files.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Levels: User home dot Claude, Claude dot M D (personal), Project Claude dot M D or the dot Claude Claude dot M D file (shared), Directory subfolder files. Modular: the at import syntax, the markdown files in the dot Claude rules folder topic files, slash memory to see what loaded. Commands: Project the dot Claude commands folder (shared) versus user home dot Claude commands (personal). Skills: a skill folder with a Skill dot M D file; frontmatter context: fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint. Personal variant: Own skill in home dot Claude skills under a different name. Skill versus Claude dot M D: Skill equals on demand, task-specific; Claude dot M D equals always loaded, universal. Path rules: the dot Claude rules folderx dot M D with paths: globs (for example any test T S X file); loads only for matching files.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A new engineer says Claude Code does not follow the team's standards, but it does for the lead developer. The lead put the standards in home dot Claude, Claude dot M D. What is the fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. User-level files apply only to that user; project-level files travel with the repository.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A root Claude dot M D has grown to eight hundred lines covering testing, A P I design and deployment. Which change keeps instructions maintainable? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Topic-specific rule files give a modular alternative to a monolithic file.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A monorepo has packages that each need different standards documents. How can each package's Claude dot M D include only the right ones? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. the at import syntax pulls in selected files and keeps each file modular.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Claude behaves differently between two sessions on the same repository. How can you check what instructions were loaded? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. slash memory shows the loaded memory files and helps diagnose inconsistency.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. The team wants a or release-check command that runs its standard release checklist and should be available to every developer who clones the repository. Where should the command file go? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Project-scoped commands in the repository are version-controlled and shared.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A skill that analyzes a whole codebase prints thousands of lines and clutters the main conversation. Which frontmatter helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. context: fork runs the skill in an isolated context and returns only its summary.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. A skill needs a required package name but developers often run it with no argument. Which option prompts for it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. argument-hint shows what parameter is expected when the skill is invoked without arguments.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. A developer wants a personal variation of a shared skill without changing it for teammates. What should they do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. A personal skill under a different name leaves teammates unaffected.

2.title: Practice Question 9
2.text: Question nine. Test files (.test.tsx) sit next to components all over the codebase, and all of them must follow the same testing conventions automatically. What is the most maintainable setup? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Glob-scoped rules apply by file pattern wherever the files are and load only when needed.

2.title: Practice Question 10
2.text: Question ten. Which content belongs in the always-loaded Claude dot M D, not in a skill? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Always-loaded context is for universal standards; task-specific workflows suit on-demand skills.

2.title: Practice Question 11
2.text: Question eleven. Select two. Which two statements about path-specific rules are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and E. A glob in the rule's frontmatter scopes it to matching files wherever they are, and it loads only when needed. It is not limited to one directory and needs no command.

2.title: Practice Question 12
2.text: Question twelve. Select two. Which two belong in the user-level home dot Claude, Claude dot M D? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and E. User-level instructions are personal and not shared. Standards, testing rules and release steps for the team belong at project level.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all twelve answers. Question one: B. Question two: B. Question three: B. Question four: D. Question five: C. Question six: C. Question seven: D. Question eight: C. Question nine: A. Question ten: C. Question eleven: B and E. Question twelve: B and E. In the next module, we continue the course.
